physicalNotes: Radius 1.051 Jupiter radii from Lillo-Box et al. 2026 (2026arXiv260719756L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260719756L/abstract): 75,138.1 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 5.92 Jupiter masses (Lillo-Box et al. 2026, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2026arXiv260719756L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260719756L/abstract) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Lillo-Box et al. 2026 (2026arXiv260719756L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname LILLO_BOX_ET_AL_2026): P 4.4331824 d
sources.shape: Lillo-Box et al. 2026 (2026arXiv260719756L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname LILLO_BOX_ET_AL_2026): a/R* 9.17; Lillo-Box et al. 2026 (2026arXiv260719756L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname LILLO_BOX_ET_AL_2026): inclination 88.78 degrees

sources.phase: Lillo-Box et al. 2026 (2026arXiv260719756L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname LILLO_BOX_ET_AL_2026): transit mid-time 2460555.31972 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 1 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
